title: Sayings and idioms
job: The figurative everyday, and when it is used
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

allowedPatterns: Ne nádo délat' iz múkhi sloná
Ni púkha ni perá + ! + — + K chyórtu + !
U menyá rúki ne dokhódyat do + <N-genitive>
Ya sevódnya ne v svoyéy tarélke

rules.text: THE FROZEN PHRASE, and the law is that it does not inflect. Four levels have taught you that Russian agrees — that a noun takes the case its slot asks for and an adjective follows it. An idiom is the one place that stops. ni púkha ni perá is a genitive that answers to no verb in your sentence; s lyógkim párom is an instrumental with nothing to govern it; ne v svoyéy tarélke keeps its own ne inside. None of them may be re-cased, re-ordered, made plural or negated from outside. Learn each one as a single long word that happens to be written with spaces.

TWO OF THESE DEMAND AN ANSWER, and the answer is fixed. ni púkha ni perá is answered K chyórtu — to the devil — and by nothing else. s lyógkim párom is answered spasíbo, and by nothing else. This is why a course teaches idioms instead of listing them: an idiom with an obligatory reply is a two-turn item, and knowing only the first turn leaves you silent at the moment you are spoken to.

AN ENGLISH IDIOM TRANSLATED WORD FOR WORD PRODUCES NOTHING IN RUSSIAN — not a wrong sentence, not a foreign-sounding one, just noise. There is no Russian gora out of a molehill and no Russian peas in a pod. The reverse is also true, which is why the literal line under each hero here reads as nonsense on purpose. And the sharpest case is the reply: answering ni púkha ni perá with spasíbo is grammatical, polite and wrong — thanking for the wish is held to cancel it, and it is the single most visible foreign move in this module.

THE PICTURE OFTEN CARRIES OVER, with the animals changed, and that is free money. délat' iz múkhi sloná is making a mountain out of a molehill with a fly and an elephant. kak dve kápli vodý is two peas in a pod with two drops of water. A learner who is shown the picture keeps the phrase, so read the literal line first and the cue second.

REACH AND REGISTER decide half of when you may say these. rúki ne dokhódyat is what anybody says to anybody at any moment. s lyógkim párom belongs to exactly one situation — somebody has just come out of a bath or a banya — and said anywhere else it is a joke. And none of these is a poslovitsa: a full-sentence proverb like Tíshe yédesh', dál'she búdesh' is a different genre, quoted rather than used, and this course does not teach it.

sentences.display: Ya vsyó sdélal, i délo v shlyápe.
sentences.script: Я всё сделал, и дело в шляпе.
sentences.cue: I've done everything, and it's in the bag.
sentences.literal: I everything did, and business in hat.

words.note: Frozen: the business is in the hat — a job finished and safe. One lexeme written with spaces, never re-cased and never plural, whatever the sentence around it does.

sentences.trap: It reports a result, not a plan. Said before you have finished, it sounds like boasting; said after, it is exactly right.
sentences.sound: The v leans forward onto the next word, so the last three come out as one breath: DYEH-la fshLYAH-pye.

variations.display: Oná vsyó sdélala, i délo v shlyápe.
variations.script: Она всё сделала, и дело в шляпе.
variations.cue: She's done everything, and it's in the bag.
variations.changed: the subject, so the past tense takes its feminine -a — the idiom itself does not move

variations.display: Vsyó sdélal — i délo v shlyápe.
variations.script: Всё сделал — и дело в шляпе.
variations.cue: All done — and it's in the bag.
variations.changed: the pronoun dropped, which is how it is actually said out loud

mistake.display: Ya vsyó sdélal, i déla v shlyápakh.
mistake.script: Я всё сделал, и дела в шляпах.
mistake.why: Made plural because the jobs were plural. The idiom does not agree with anything — it is délo v shlyápe for one job, ten jobs or a whole year's work.

sentences.usage: Telling a friend the job is done and nothing can go wrong now.
sentences.mnemonic: The answer was hidden in the hat — once it is in there, it is settled.

sentences.display: Ne nádo délat' iz múkhi sloná.
sentences.script: Не надо делать из мухи слона.
sentences.cue: Don't make a mountain out of a molehill.
sentences.literal: Not necessary to-make out-of fly elephant.

words.cue: to make a mountain out of a molehill
words.note: The one idiom here whose verb still conjugates: délat' becomes délayesh', délayet. The tail iz múkhi sloná never moves. Bare délat' is L2-M8's row.

sentences.trap: The English picture is a molehill and a mountain; the Russian one is a fly and an elephant. Carry the picture across, never the words.
sentences.sound: múkhi opens with the rough kh of Scottish loch, and sloná puts its stress on the last syllable: slah-NAH.

variations.display: Ty vsegdá délayesh' iz múkhi sloná.
variations.script: Ты всегда делаешь из мухи слона.
variations.cue: You always make a mountain out of a molehill.
variations.changed: the verb conjugated to ty — the only part of this idiom that is allowed to move

variations.display: On délayet iz múkhi sloná.
variations.script: Он делает из мухи слона.
variations.cue: He makes a mountain out of a molehill.
variations.changed: third person, with the frozen tail untouched

mistake.display: Ne nádo délat' iz mukh slonóv.
mistake.script: Не надо делать из мух слонов.
mistake.why: Both animals pluralised to match a lot of fuss. The count is fixed at one fly and one elephant however big the fuss is.

sentences.usage: Telling a friend, kindly, that the thing they are upset about is small.
sentences.mnemonic: One fly in, one elephant out — the animals never change number.

sentences.display: U menyá rúki ne dokhódyat do rabóty.
sentences.script: У меня руки не доходят до работы.
sentences.cue: I never get round to the work.
sentences.literal: At me hands not reach up-to work.

words.cue: I never get round to it
words.note: Literally the hands do not reach. Always plural rúki, always with its own ne; what is not reached follows do in the genitive. Bare rúki is L3-M7's body row.

sentences.trap: It is an excuse about time, not about ability. It says the day ran out, never that the job was too hard.
sentences.sound: dokhódyat carries the same rough kh as múkhi, and the final -yat is a light dyet with no stress on it.

variations.display: Rúki ne dokhódyat do rabóty.
variations.script: Руки не доходят до работы.
variations.cue: I never get round to the work.
variations.changed: u menyá dropped — with no owner named it is understood as the speaker's

variations.display: Sevódnya u menyá rúki ne dokhódyat do rabóty.
variations.script: Сегодня у меня руки не доходят до работы.
variations.cue: Today I'm not getting round to the work.
variations.changed: sevódnya in front, narrowing an always to a today

mistake.display: U menyá ruká ne dokhódit do rabóty.
mistake.script: У меня рука не доходит до работы.
mistake.why: Singularised, because English says my hand. The idiom is fixed in the plural, and one hand not reaching is a sentence about an arm.

sentences.usage: Apologising for something you keep meaning to do and never do.
sentences.mnemonic: Two hands, both busy, neither of them reaching that far.

sentences.display: U menyá vsegdá rúki ne dokhódyat do písem.
sentences.script: У меня всегда руки не доходят до писем.
sentences.cue: I never get round to my letters.
sentences.literal: At me always hands not reach up-to letters.

words.note: Genitive plural of pis'mó, first taught in L1-M5. do asks for the genitive, and this is the shape it wants: do písem, as far as the letters.

sentences.trap: do takes the genitive here as it always has. The noun after it is never the dictionary form, so pis'mó cannot stand in this slot.
sentences.sound: písem is two syllables with the stress on the first, and the e in the ending is a light ye: PEE-syem.

variations.display: Rúki ne dokhódyat do písem.
variations.script: Руки не доходят до писем.
variations.cue: I never get round to the letters.
variations.changed: the owner dropped, leaving the bare complaint

variations.display: U menyá rúki ne dokhódyat do písem i do rabóty.
variations.script: У меня руки не доходят до писем и до работы.
variations.cue: I get round to neither the letters nor the work.
variations.changed: two things not reached, joined with i and each keeping its own do

mistake.display: U menyá rúki ne dokhódyat do pis'mó.
mistake.script: У меня руки не доходят до письмо.
mistake.why: The dictionary form left standing after do. The preposition governs the genitive, so it has to be do písem — or do pis'má for a single letter.

sentences.usage: Explaining to a friend why nobody has heard from you.
sentences.mnemonic: do is a reach towards something, and what you reach towards is always genitive.

sentences.display: Ya sevódnya ne v svoyéy tarélke.
sentences.script: Я сегодня не в своей тарелке.
sentences.literal: I today not in own plate.

words.note: Not in one's own plate — off form, not oneself today. The ne lives inside the idiom, so it is never dropped and never moved out in front of the verb.

sentences.trap: It reports a mood, not an illness and not a place. If you are actually ill, this is not the sentence.
sentences.sound: svoyéy is two syllables, svah-YAY, and tarélke ends in a light -kye rather than a hard -ke.

variations.display: Oná sevódnya ne v svoyéy tarélke.
variations.script: Она сегодня не в своей тарелке.
variations.cue: She's not herself today.
variations.changed: the subject only — svoyéy already means whosever the sentence is, so nothing inside the idiom changes

variations.display: Ya ne v svoyéy tarélke.
variations.script: Я не в своей тарелке.
variations.cue: I'm not myself.
variations.changed: the day dropped, leaving it open-ended

mistake.display: Ya sevódnya ne v moyéy tarélke.
mistake.script: Я сегодня не в моей тарелке.
mistake.why: svoyéy swapped for moyéy because English says my. The idiom is frozen with svoyéy, and it stays svoyéy whoever the subject is.

sentences.usage: Warning a friend, gently, that you are poor company today.
sentences.mnemonic: Everyone has their own plate; today you are eating off somebody else's.

sentences.display: Oná i yeyó sestrá kak dve kápli vodý.
sentences.script: Она и её сестра как две капли воды.
sentences.cue: She and her sister are as alike as two peas in a pod.
sentences.literal: She and her sister like two drops of-water.

words.cue: as alike as two peas in a pod
words.note: Like two drops of water — the English two peas in a pod with the picture changed. Frozen at two drops: never three, never kápli vodá.

sentences.trap: It is about looking alike, not about thinking alike. Two people who agree about everything are not kak dve kápli vodý.
sentences.sound: vodý takes its stress on the last syllable, vah-DYH, which is not where L2-M3's vodá put it.

variations.display: Moyá sestrá i ya kak dve kápli vodý.
variations.script: Моя сестра и я как две капли воды.
variations.cue: My sister and I are as alike as two peas in a pod.
variations.changed: the pair being compared — the idiom is untouched

variations.display: Mat' i sestrá kak dve kápli vodý.
variations.script: Мать и сестра как две капли воды.
variations.cue: Mother and sister are as alike as two peas in a pod.
variations.changed: two nouns instead of a pronoun and a noun, with no verb needed between them

mistake.display: Oná i yeyó sestrá kak tri kápli vodý.
mistake.script: Она и её сестра как три капли воды.
mistake.why: Three drops for three sisters. The number is part of the phrase and does not count the people — it stays dve however many are alike.

sentences.usage: Remarking on a family resemblance you have just noticed.
sentences.mnemonic: Two drops of water, and nobody can say which one is which.

sentences.display: Závtra u menyá ekzámen, i ya ne v svoyéy tarélke.
sentences.script: Завтра у меня экзамен, и я не в своей тарелке.
sentences.cue: I have an exam tomorrow, and I'm not myself.
sentences.literal: Tomorrow at me exam, and I not in own plate.

words.note: An exam. Masculine, stressed in the middle, and the thing ni púkha ni perá is wished at more often than anything else in Russian.

sentences.trap: u menyá ekzámen is how Russian says I have an exam — no verb at all, exactly as L1-M8 taught it.
sentences.sound: The opening ek- is a plain e as in bed, and the stress lands on the middle: ek-ZAH-myen.

variations.display: Závtra u menyá ekzámen.
variations.script: Завтра у меня экзамен.
variations.cue: I have an exam tomorrow.
variations.changed: the second clause dropped, leaving the bare fact

variations.display: Sevódnya u menyá ekzámen, i ya ne v svoyéy tarélke.
variations.script: Сегодня у меня экзамен, и я не в своей тарелке.
variations.cue: I have an exam today, and I'm not myself.
variations.changed: the day, and nothing else

mistake.display: Závtra ya iméyu ekzámen, i ya ne v svoyéy tarélke.
mistake.script: Завтра я имею экзамен, и я не в своей тарелке.
mistake.why: An English have dragged into Russian. Possession is u menyá plus the thing; a verb here reads as a translation, not as speech.

sentences.usage: Telling a friend why you are on edge, and inviting the wish that answers it.
sentences.mnemonic: The exam is tomorrow, so the plate is somebody else's today.

sentences.display: Ni púkha ni perá! — K chyórtu!
sentences.script: Ни пуха ни пера! — К чёрту!
sentences.literal: Neither fluff nor feather! — To devil!

words.note: Neither fluff nor feather — a hunter's wish for a bad bag, said to trick the luck. Said BEFORE the trial, never after, and it governs nothing in your sentence.
The one legal reply to ni púkha ni perá, and it is not rude. Bare k is L3-M7's; here it is welded to chyórtu and the pair is never split.

sentences.trap: Answering spasíbo is the visible foreign move. Thanking for the wish is held to cancel it, so the reply that sounds rudest is the polite one.
sentences.sound: chyórtu is the yó of L1's yólka — CHOR-too — and the k in front of it is a single consonant leaning on the word.

variations.display: Ni púkha ni perá!
variations.script: Ни пуха ни пера!
variations.cue: Good luck!
variations.changed: only the wish, when the answer will come a beat later

variations.display: Závtra ekzámen. Ni púkha ni perá!
variations.script: Завтра экзамен. Ни пуха ни пера!
variations.cue: The exam's tomorrow. Good luck!
variations.changed: the reason said out loud before the wish

mistake.why: The polite English answer, and the one answer Russian does not allow here. Thanking accepts the luck and is said to undo it; the reply is K chyórtu.

sentences.usage: Wishing a friend luck the night before an exam, an interview or a first day.
sentences.mnemonic: Wish them nothing, and they are sent to the devil for it — that is how the luck is fooled.

sentences.cue: Enjoy that just-bathed feeling! — Thank you!

words.cue: said to someone fresh from a bath
words.note: With light steam — said to somebody who has just bathed, and only then. An instrumental with no verb over it, and the reply is spasíbo and nothing else.

sentences.trap: This one has a single situation. Said to somebody who has not just bathed, it is a joke, and everybody hears it as one.
sentences.sound: lyógkim carries the yó, and the g in it is said as a k: LYOKH-kyeem, párom stressed on the first syllable.

variations.display: S lyógkim párom!
variations.script: С лёгким паром!
variations.cue: Enjoy that just-bathed feeling!
variations.changed: the wish on its own, before the answer comes

variations.display: Ty dóma? S lyógkim párom!
variations.script: Ты дома? С лёгким паром!
variations.cue: You're home? Enjoy that just-bathed feeling!
variations.changed: a question in front of it, the way it lands in a real doorway

mistake.why: The right reply to the wrong wish. K chyórtu answers ni púkha ni perá only; this pair is answered spasíbo.

sentences.usage: Greeting somebody stepping out of the bath or back from the banya.
sentences.mnemonic: Light steam, light thanks — this is the pair where spasíbo is correct.

sentences.display: Ty iz vánnoy? S lyógkim párom!
sentences.script: Ты из ванной? С лёгким паром!
sentences.cue: Out of the bath? Enjoy that fresh feeling!
sentences.literal: You out-of bathroom? With light steam!

words.note: The bathroom in the shape iz asks for: iz vánnoy, out of the bathroom. It is an adjective by origin, which is why it ends like one rather than like a noun.

sentences.trap: vánnoy is the room; the wish is about the wash. Somebody who went in to find a towel does not get greeted with it.
sentences.sound: The double n is held a moment longer than a single one, VAHN-nay, and the ending is a light -ay.

variations.display: Ty iz vánnoy?
variations.script: Ты из ванной?
variations.cue: Are you out of the bath?
variations.changed: the question alone, with the wish held back

variations.display: Ya iz vánnoy.
variations.script: Я из ванной.
variations.cue: I'm out of the bath.
variations.changed: the answer from the other side of the door

mistake.display: Ty iz vánnaya? S lyógkim párom!
mistake.script: Ты из ванная? С лёгким паром!
mistake.why: The dictionary form left standing after iz. iz governs the genitive, and for this adjective-shaped noun that is vánnoy.

sentences.usage: Meeting somebody in the hall as they come out of the bathroom.
sentences.mnemonic: Out of the room, into the wish — iz vánnoy, then s lyógkim párom.
